newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul business body says August BSI down from July.
newsitem.headline: Seoul business body says August BSI down from July.

text.p: The Federation of Korean Industries said on Thursday the all-industry Business Survey Index for August was 85.8, down from 89.7 for July.
An index of less than 100 means the outlook is negative.
The federation attributed the drop in the index to weakening purchasing power as a result of the economic slump and slowing demand for durable goods.
The federation is South Korea's biggest private industry organisation representing most of the nation's leading conglomerates, known as chaebols.
The index had been improving since it bottomed out at 74.1 in April, rising to 78.4 in May and 80.1 in June, it said.
It also said the recovery in exports was seen to be delayed by the Japanese yen's renewed weakness against the U.S. dollar and expected more fallout from continuing corporate crises.
Earlier this month the nation's eighth-largest Kia Group was tapped for bailout by creditor banks because banks thought the group would be unable to avoid defaulting on debt payments.

Analysts say the group's troubles were expected to damage the international image of not only the group, whose flagship is one of the nation's leading carmakers Kia Motors Corp , but South Korean products in general.

South Korean exports are also expected to be affected by slowing import demand in southeast Asian markets following the recent effective devaluations of the Thai and Philippine currencies, the report said.
